newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FEATURE - If water is golden, tap BWT analysts say.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - If water is golden, tap BWT analysts say.

text.p: If you believe apocalyptic voices that say water will be the next century's scarce commodity, like oil and precious stones and metals, then pouring your money into a water treatment company would be a canny investment.

Water seems to be in abundance -- it covers more than two thirds of the world. But more than 97 percent is sea water and a further 2.2 percent is in polar ice, glaciers and the air, leaving just 0.6 percent for immediate consumption.

And with Europe's population draining the continent's reserves, analysts forecast that the global market for water technology will almost double in the next 10 years because of the growing need for water purification.

The leading manufacturer of such technology in Europe is Austria's BWT AG, also known as Best Water Technology. BWT is based just outside Salzburg and has a total of 22 subsidiaries in Europe employing 1,358 people.
Analysts recommend BWT as a long-term buy not only for its market leadership and innovative drive, but also because the stock offers a significant valuation discount to its European and U.S. peers.
"Looking at price/earnings valuations, BWT is certainly cheaper than the market average and also significantly cheaper than its rivals," said First Austrian analyst Andreas Riegler.

BWT's biggest rival is U.S. Filter Corp, 10 times the size of BWT in terms of market capitalisation with more than double the workforce. But the U.S. titan looks expensive on a price/earnings (PE) ratio of 57.4 times versus BWT's 15, according to data on Reuters Securities 3000.
"Long-term BWT's certainly a buy. It has an environmental appeal -- a so-called 'green share'," said Roland Neuwirth, an analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Vienna.

"The market is now hoping for at least double-digit growth in earnings and sales -- so if one expects such growth in the next few years then one can by all means grant BWT a significantly higher PE," he added.
A consensus of seven analysts, compiled by Edinburgh Financial Publishing, forecasts earnings per share of 110 schillings ($9) this year after 106 schillings in 1996 and 103 in 1995.
And for 1998, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is looking for EPS of 128, First Austrian of 130, while Investmentbank Austria expects EPS of 133.
SHARE PRICE MOVEMENTS
BWT's share price has already had a good run this year, surging over 50 percent after spending the last year hemmed into a claustrophobic trading range.

The rally was sparked by news in March that the company would develop a new technology that treats household water. Another factor was the reception, and subsequent orders, of the new product at an industrial fair in Germany.
"This new product AQA Total has grabbed the imagination of investors," said Wolfgang Pinner, head of research at Investmentbank Austria.

BWT chairman Andreas Weissenbacher said the product, which prevents the build-up of lime without the use of chemicals and salt and thereby protects the environment -- and the life of domestic appliances -- was expected to bring in extra sales of 700 million schillings in 2001.

Weissenbacher sees AQA Total generating earnings of some 56 million schillings on sales of around 200 million next year. Development and marketing costs were expected to weigh down earnings a touch this year, he added.

BWT reported record earnings in 1996, with group pretax profit jumping 21 percent to 231.1 million schillings and sales rising eight percent to 2.32 billion. BWT sees sales climbing to 2.5 billion this year.
The group will pay an unchanged dividend of 27 schillings, but plans to raise this to 28 in 1997, Weissenbacher said.

Analysts point out that the flotation of Christ, the Swiss project technology group whose share capital is 26 percent owned by BWT and 26 percent by Christ's management, released BWT from a heavy investment burden and improved the financial position of Christ.

On Friday, BWT broke through its all-time high of 1,850 schillings, recorded in 1994, to trade around 1,855. Traders said the rally broke out after the shares pierced key resistance of 1,700 on Thursday.
BWT is tipped to be included in the Vienna Stock Exchange's blue-chip ATX index due to the relatively high liquidity of the issue.
($ = 12.16 Austrian Schillings)
